question: A stationery seller purchases 6 notebooks for ₹30 and sells them for ₹36. What is his profit percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Cost Price to Selling Price = 30 : 36 = 5 : 6

Profit = 6 − 5 = 1 unit

Profit % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of 6 notebooks = ₹30

Selling Price (SP) of 6 notebooks = ₹36

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 CP = ₹30 SP = ₹36 
• 
 + ₹6 Profit Profit % = (6 ÷ 30) × 100 = 20% 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit = 36 − 30 = ₹6

⇒ Profit % = (6 ÷ 30) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Discount

For successive discounts of a% and b%, the Effective Discount = a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100 %.

Dishonest Dealer

The profit percentage is always calculated based on the actual quantity of goods handed over to the buyer, not on the promised quantity.
